comparison: Same 362-file accepted fixture and 30 registered checks; real fs/crypto/zlib/Buffer.equals calls are counted. No elapsed-time threshold or estimated byte-iteration count.

names: incomplete in-process h11 [X] bad-chunk-size: typed refusal after the earlier answers, then the connection is closed and no slot is kept
a request whose message is complete (a Content-Length body) is answered before the refusal behind it, the submit still in flight
a request whose message is complete (a chunked body) is answered before the refusal behind it, the submit still in flight
a refused connection is destroyed at the flush of the refusal, not left to Node: destroy() runs while the socket has not finished its own shutdown
a body that arrives slowly is not refused: the incomplete check applies only after the client error, and the connection stays usable
a queued request whose body is still arriving when its turn comes is served, not dropped: only a client error makes an incomplete request refused
